basis: Central and peripheral neurodegeneration define disease; amyotrophy reflects denervation rather than intrinsic muscle disease. Optic atrophy and scoliosis occur in 5-29%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: amyotrophy in 80-99% reflects motor-neuron denervation; intrinsic muscle disease is not established, and scoliosis occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Inherited protein C deficiency is a coagulation disorder. DVT occurs in 4/9 but is a separately diagnosed thrombotic complication; other organ damage frequencies are unspecified.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: recurrent DVT occurs in 4/9 (~44%), but is a separately diagnosed complication of the underlying thrombophilia.

basis: BH4 synthesis deficiency causes hyperphenylalaninemia and central neurotransmitter depletion; progressive cognitive and motor deficits are explicitly defining, with developmental delay in 11/12.

decisions.neurologic: primary: progressive cognitive and motor deficits are explicitly part of the disease definition; developmental delay occurs in 11/12 (~92%).

basis: Ophthalmoplegia/ptosis, mouth malformation and preauricular skin tags define the syndrome. Actual tragus hypoplasia occurs in only 5-29%; hearing impairment is not established.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: preauricular skin tags are a named defining cutaneous malformation, reported in 30-79%.
decisions.otologic: none: preauricular skin tags and pits do not establish external-ear dysfunction; actual tragus hypoplasia occurs in only 5-29%.

basis: Congenital NMJ dysfunction defines CMS22. Growth hormone deficiency is a characteristic common PREPL-deficiency feature (>30%; exact prevalence uncertain); weakness and ptosis reflect NMJ dysfunction.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: involved: growth hormone deficiency is a characteristic common feature of PREPL deficiency (>30% in reported clinical experience); this record gives no precise frequency.

basis: Metabolic bone disease defined by reduced bone mass and disrupted cortical/trabecular architecture, causing skeletal fragility; endocrine causes need not be present.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: osteoporosis is a metabolic bone disorder of bone remodeling, explicitly supported by its parent; the mechanism axis does not require an endocrine cause.

basis: ID, muscle/skeletal defects and lung hypoplasia define the syndrome; lung hypoplasia and strabismus each occur in 80-99%. Dental anomalies in 30-79% are omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: hypoplastic bronchial/lung development is an explicit defining structural malformation, with lung hypoplasia reported in 80-99%.

basis: Renal dysgenesis, thymic aplasia and anal atresia define the syndrome. Named lung dysplasia qualifies as a core malformation despite unspecified frequency; the three-primary cap places it in involved.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: lung dysplasia is a named core malformation, satisfying the defining-feature exception despite unspecified frequency; three primary axes are retained.
decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: anal dysplasia/atresia is a named defining malformation, corroborated by the anal-atresia HPO annotation.

basis: Severe growth restriction and skeletal dysmorphism define the phenotype. No endocrine dysfunction is established; developmental delay occurs in 1/4 (25%) and cardiac defects in 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: growth restriction and IGF2 association alone do not establish endocrine gland dysfunction or a metabolic disorder in the supplied phenotype.

basis: Inherited immunodeficiency; autoimmune cytopenias, lymphoma and bronchiectasis are separately diagnosed diseases. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish organ damage.

decisions.haematologic: none: autoimmune hemolytic anemia (2/2), thrombocytopenia (1/2) and lymphoma (2/2) are separately diagnosed diseases arising with the immunodeficiency.
